summary:
HeatWatch is a web-based Earth Temperature Monitoring System developed by Team White Universe for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It allows users to explore temperature information through geographical maps and displayed temperature values.

Our project addresses the challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” by making temperature information easier to explore and understand across different geographical locations. The map-based interface helps users observe temperature variations between regions and improves awareness of Earth's changing environmental conditions.

Understanding temperature patterns is important because temperature changes can affect ecosystems, climate, agriculture, and human activities. HeatWatch aims to make environmental information more accessible and encourage users to explore Earth's temperature conditions.

Future improvements include historical temperature analysis, regional trend comparison, and statistical analysis to identify significant long-term changes.
details:
1. What Does the Project Do?

HeatWatch is a web-based Earth Temperature Monitoring System developed by Team White Universe. It allows users to explore temperature information through geographical maps and displayed temperature values. The platform provides a simple way to view temperature conditions across different geographical locations.

2. How Does It Work?

HeatWatch presents temperature information through a map-based interface. Users can explore geographical areas and view the temperature values displayed by the application. This makes environmental information easier to access and understand.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

HeatWatch aims to improve awareness of Earth's temperature conditions and encourage people to explore environmental information. Understanding temperature variations across geographical locations is important because temperature changes can influence ecosystems, agriculture, climate conditions, and human activities.

The project aims to make temperature information more accessible through a simple and user-friendly interface.

4. Tools and Technologies Used

The technologies used in developing HeatWatch include:

  • HTML – for structuring the web application.
  • CSS – for styling and designing the interface.
  • JavaScript – for application functionality and interaction.
  • Leaflet.js – for displaying interactive geographical maps.
  • NASA POWER API – include this only if it is actually connected and used in your application.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The main creative aspect of HeatWatch is its map-based approach to exploring temperature information. Instead of presenting only numerical values, it combines temperature information with geographical visualization. This helps users connect environmental data with real-world locations.

6. Factors Considered by the Team

Our team focused on simplicity, usability, geographical visualization, and environmental awareness while developing the project. We aimed to create an interface that makes temperature information easy to explore and understand.

7. Future Improvements

Future development may include historical temperature graphs, regional trend comparisons, statistical analysis of temperature changes, and additional Earth-system variables. These improvements could help users identify long-term patterns and understand environmental changes more effectively.
